messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Bug in DISTANCE 6.0:  Estimation of encounter rate variance
parts:
List,

Further to Tim Ritter's report of a problem with CDS point transect variance
estimation, we have confirmed that this is a Bug with the R2 estimator, have
fixed it, and will be issuing a new release of Distance shortly.

The bug report is here:
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=92
More details (from the bug report response) is given below.

- Len Thomas

From
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=92

The problem was that for estimator P2, a routine was returning the variance of
the estimated encounter rate, when it should have been the standard error --
i.e., a square root was not being taken.

Typically the standard error on encounter rate will be less than 1, and hence
the variance is smaller than the SE, and hence using variance instead of
standard error has caused Distance to report a SE and CV that is smaller than it
should be.

We will issue a new release of Distance shortly. Since P2 is the default
estimator of encounter rate variance, we recommend that CDS and MCDS point
transect analyses that were run in Distance 6.0 Release 1 and 2 be re-run in
the new release to check the analytic variance estimator.

We apologize for any problems caused by this bug.


--
Len Thomas, Co-ordinator, Distance Development Project
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Centre for Research into Environmental and Ecological Modelling
